relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP-variant carrier with Alexander disease: "Analysis of the GFAPgene revealed a heterozygous missense mutation, c.827G>T, p.R276L".
method_note: Single-patient case report, read and transcribed by hand (a short Python script only assembled the JSON and the 20 checklist rows per person). Literature persons included under the v4 passing-mention rule only where the Discussion gives an individual-level fact beyond diagnosis: ref [11] patient (variant c.827G>T, p.R276L, pathologically proven), ref [30] asymptomatic carrier (over age 60), ref [22] patient (symmetrical striatal lesions), patient 1 of ref [21] (parkinsonism), ref [32] patient (valproate-induced parkinsonism). Not given rows: 'diffuse bradykinesia [22]' (not stated to be the same person as the ref [22] striatal-lesion patient, so not attributed), 'spotty lesions [19]', 'bilateral lesions in the lateral putamen [30]' and 'rigidity of the arms [29]' (findings cited to a reference without a stated person; [30] lesions not attributed to the asymptomatic carrier), and the E223Q patient of ref [38] (variant dismissed by the authors as a polymorphism; person not diagnosed with ALX). Table 1 is a group-level literature summary (counts only) and was not used for any person. Patient age at onset left 'not reported': first symptoms (character change, dementia, dysarthria) followed head trauma at 46 and the authors say dementia cannot be considered an ALX symptom because of the contusion; spastic paresis began at 57. Feature onsets after the accident are recorded as 'After head trauma ... at the age of 46' without an ISO value. Cerebellar ataxia was 'ambiguous' per the paper, so the ataxia checklist item is not reported; gaze-evoked nystagmus is recorded under eye movement abnormality. 'Palatal myoclonus' absent was used to exclude the palatal tremor item. Cerebral white matter abnormality marked observed on the basis of deep white matter lacunae, although leukoencephalopathy was explicitly absent (lacunae may not be disease-related). Laboratory tests 'unremarkable' recorded as the paper words it (general investigation; nothing more specific excluded). Hedged 'rigid-bradykinesia type parkinsonism' for the patient not recorded. Contradictions/inconsistencies: the Case Presentation calls the mutation 'heterogeneous' while Abstract and Discussion say 'heterozygous' (heterozygous recorded); text says 'slight cerebral atrophy' but Figure 1 legend says 'moderate cortical atrophy' (both quoted in one row's severity); text says the pontine base was spared/intact while the figure legend says 'little atrophy of the pontine base' (no pontine row emitted). Inheritance not reported: sporadic case with no family history, parents not tested. Variant in exon 5. Ref [11] patient's variant row takes type and pathogenicity from the sentence naming that exact variant; zygosity not reported for that person.
